task.name: A resumed sprint routes on the live forge.yaml while reporting that stories run under the pinned snapshot
task.story_text:
## Observed

Sprint `issues-2775,2906,2908,2909,2913,2914` was launched 2026-09-05 and pinned its config as `forge.yaml e347869eff1f` (snapshot `.forge/sprints/0b59d0d851f1/forge.yaml`). Between launch and resume the project-root `forge.yaml` was edited and committed to add a new inline model (`anthropic/fable/cli`) and new `assignment.exploration` values.

On `--resume` (2026-09-06, run `68aec168166d`) the sprint logged, at start and again before each story:

```
⚠ forge.yaml in the project root changed after this sprint pinned its config (pinned e347869eff1f, now d27bf7274488); stories keep running under the pinned snapshot
↺ WORKSPACE   synced forge.yaml from sprint-pinned snapshot .forge/sprints/0b59d0d851f1/forge.yaml
```

The pinned snapshot contains no `fable` entry and no `exploration` block (grepped). Yet in the same resumed run the router seated `anthropic-fable-cli` as a code reviewer on `issue-2913` (it ran, $1.19) and on `issue-2914` (persisted in `.forge/routing/issue-2914.json` and in the `routing_decision.code_review.candidate_pool` of audit `e4a8af6e2cc8`). A model that exists only in the post-pin root config was dispatched by a run that reported itself as executing under the pre-pin snapshot.

## Expected

A sprint runs under one configuration. Whatever surface the operator is told is authoritative for a run — the pinned snapshot, here — is the configuration every part of that run reads: the model registry the router selects from, the exploration and assignment settings it applies, and the `forge.yaml` synced into each worktree. When the root config drifts after pinning, either the whole run keeps the snapshot or the whole run adopts the new one and says so; a run must never report one config while any component of it reads another. An audit reader who opens the pinned snapshot must be able to account for every model the run dispatched.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `c006f6cb125918c166574b689ddfd0d67f3066ea` captured at `2026-09-07T08:39:53.062008+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/cli/sprint.py` — `sha256:1a9f179015dcc7aeddff58264cb62657800b875811f094f39c9f5300cc5fe40b`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:04194d575614371d80ad71f1779d5d1fd1b8bc79c3d419639171ac9712aaf6fb`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/config_snapshot.py` — `sha256:1cc62b07b6d3c26e159523a5fca3a944d0d66655a83218b10c7392ebb9f28a37`
- `src/theforge/assignment.py` — `sha256:7f51b053f63685ad3046b3c0a9c35598d88ea21f0f114b094651b34462bcfa2f`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight.py` — `sha256:f85fa1c79a8a89a5581e83c0d0aaec8246392c948888bba936542cc0332349d2`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/review_phase.py` — `sha256:ad67a25d55433656735adfed9b905f60808d7713b5178dbcca8d17a285cd7833`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/plan_flow.py` — `sha256:510cef81d4e23e1927b6b5c2f0fb21416b3acf9f99fd993fc1f8025fcd5ab68d`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py` — `sha256:667c57c328172787c6bcae2675ee0d014633ba78c32090083bf8666704a6a0a9`
- `forge.yaml` — `sha256:d27bf7274488ee1732a643b3b887da16063a240a02cc760d4c60b43f07fbfd01`
- `.forge/sprints/0b59d0d851f1/forge.yaml` — `sha256:e347869eff1f9505fc5fa1e9871b2775b8d2eb4f9537d5cac68f68f68e2ebd34`
- `.forge/routing/issue-2914.json` — `sha256:de05c09240f61f38573d17ce3a30d9d7a359c7aa12d7ae99dc418f1f7807188e`
- `.forge/logs/issues-2775,2906,2908,2909,2913,2914/run-68aec168166d.log` — `sha256:d7ce3fb06e9dd65262d9586f160b6425cbf26db1187b4ea5f88065ff5695ff82`

### Observed symptom

A resumed sprint logs, at sprint entry and before each story, that the
project-root forge.yaml drifted after the sprint pinned its config and
that "stories keep running under the pinned snapshot." That claim is
only true for the per-worktree copy of forge.yaml. The router (code
reviewer selection, exploration, dev/plan model choice) actually dispatched
a model (anthropic/fable/cli) that exists only in the live, post-pin
project-root forge.yaml and is absent from the pinned snapshot the sprint
reports as authoritative — on issue-2913 (ran, $1.19) and issue-2914
(persisted in .forge/routing/issue-2914.json and audit
e4a8af6e2cc8's routing_decision.code_review.candidate_pool).

### Reproduction / evidence

- `.forge/sprints/0b59d0d851f1/forge.yaml` (pinned snapshot, digest
  e347869eff1f...) has zero occurrences of "fable" (grepped directly).
- `forge.yaml` (live project root, digest d27bf7274488...) declares a
  `fable` model entry at lines 27-36 ("Fable — Anthropic's top tier,
  added 2026-09-06 ... model: fable"), confirmed by direct grep.
- `.forge/routing/issue-2914.json` lists
  `"code_reviewers": ["gpt-5.5", "fable", "gpt-5.6-sol"]` — confirmed by
  direct read.
- Run log run-68aec168166d.log logs the drift warning and the
  "↺ WORKSPACE synced forge.yaml from sprint-pinned snapshot" line, which
  (per config_snapshot.py:301-361, read directly) affects only the
  worktree file copy, not any in-memory routing config.
- Reproduction: pin a sprint config, edit+commit a model addition to the
  root forge.yaml, `--resume` the sprint, and observe the router select a
  model from the post-pin root config for a story dispatched after resume
  while the drift-warning/worktree-sync log lines claim the pinned
  snapshot is authoritative.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree copies the wrong (live) file into the worktree despite claiming to use the pinned snapshot, so the worktree itself silently runs on live config.
  - Evidence: Read config_snapshot.py:301-361 directly. pinned_forge_yaml() reads FORGE_SPRINT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT (set by activate() to the pinned path) and sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree() copies exactly that path when present — this function correctly delivers the pinned snapshot into the worktree file.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Read the full function body at src/theforge/coordinator/config_snapshot.py:301-361 directly during this investigation.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly inspected the source; matches the prior investigation's independent finding on this same function.
- **[ruled out]** The routing candidate pool is built from the worktree's own forge.yaml post-sync, not from an in-memory config object, so a stale pre-pin worktree checkout explains the fable dispatch instead of an in-memory config gap.
  - Evidence: issue-2913 and issue-2914 dispatched fable as reviewer during the SAME resumed run that logged the pinned-snapshot sync for their worktrees. The synced worktree forge.yaml is the pinned snapshot (verified: zero 'fable' matches). If routing read the worktree file post-sync it could not have selected fable, so routing must read a config object assembled in-process before/independent of the worktree sync.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Cross-checked the routing artifact (.forge/routing/issue-2914.json) and audit e4a8af6e2cc8 against the sync log lines and the pinned snapshot file content, all read directly.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly compared the attached run log, pinned snapshot file, and routing JSON.
  - Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.
- **[confirmed]** The sprint's in-memory ForgeConfig (models.enabled, assignment.exploration, and everything routing.py/assignment.py's candidate-pool selection reads via config.assignment) is loaded once from the live project-root forge.yaml before the pin is captured/activated, and is never rebuilt from the pinned snapshot, so the router silently tracks root-file drift even though the pin (and its log messages) is correctly applied to worktree files.
  - Evidence: Traced the full call chain directly at HEAD:
1. src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:162-182 resolves config_path via
   _find_config and calls load_config_checked(config_path, ...) —
   reading the LIVE project-root forge.yaml, before any pin exists.
2. That `config` object is passed straight into
   SprintRunContext.for_sprint(config, ...) at both CLI entry paths
   (cli/sprint.py:401-402 query mode, cli/sprint.py:1403-1404
   manifest mode), becoming `_ctx.config` inside run_sprint.
3. Only afterward does run_sprint call
   `capture_or_load(_ctx.config.project_root, _ctx.sprint_id)`
   (runner.py:5492) and `config_snapshot_mod.activate(...)`
   (runner.py:5495). activate() (config_snapshot.py:251-259) does
   nothing but set/pop the FORGE_SPRINT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT env var — it
   never touches `_ctx.config` or triggers a re-parse of the pinned
   forge.yaml into a ForgeConfig object.
4. Repo-wide grep for pinned_forge_yaml/FORGE_SPRINT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT
   usage (excluding tests) finds exactly one consuming module:
   config_snapshot.py itself — specifically
   sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree(), whose own docstring says its job
   is to "place the run's operative forge.yaml in workspace_path"
   (the worktree file), not to feed the router.
5. The candidate pool / model selection (assignment.py's
   _reviewer_candidate_pool and friends) is driven by an
   `assignment_config: AssignmentConfig` parameter that in the
   coordinator is `config.assignment` (confirmed via grep across
   preflight.py, review_phase.py, plan_flow.py, engine.py — e.g.
   preflight.py:1414 `config.assignment.exploration`,
   review_phase.py:2320 `config.assignment.adaptive_enabled`) — i.e.
   the same `config`/`_ctx.config` object established in step 1-2 as
   tracing to the live root file, not to any snapshot reload.
This exactly matches the evidence: the pinned snapshot (used for the
worktree file and the drift-detection digest) has no `fable`, but the
live root forge.yaml the router actually reads does, and `fable` was
dispatched as reviewer on issue-2913/2914 in the very run that logged
the pinned-snapshot claim.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Verified directly by reading src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:162-182,392-419,1403-1432, src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:5486-5497, src/theforge/coordinator/config_snapshot.py:1-19,251-361, and by grepping config.assignment usages in preflight.py/review_phase.py/plan_flow.py/engine.py, all during this investigation.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All call-chain facts read directly from source at HEAD during this investigation. The config_snapshot.py module docstring independently corroborates the design intent (pin exists specifically so a mid-sprint root-file change cannot silently repartition a sprint, referencing #1980) but does not itself name this specific worktree-file-vs-routing-config gap, so the mechanism finding is original, not a restatement.

### Confirmed cause

The sprint pins its configuration only for worktree file preparation
(config_snapshot.capture_or_load/activate + sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree)
but never rebuilds the in-memory ForgeConfig that the router and story
dispatch use for model selection. That ForgeConfig is loaded once from the
live project-root forge.yaml in src/theforge/cli/sprint.py (via
_find_config/load_config_checked) before the pin is captured, and is
carried unchanged through SprintRunContext into run_sprint and every
per-story routing decision (config.assignment feeds
assignment.py's candidate-pool/exploration logic). config_snapshot.activate()
only sets an environment variable consumed solely by
sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree for the worktree file copy. Consequently, a
root forge.yaml edited after pinning changes what the router sees
(models.enabled, assignment.exploration, reviewer candidate pools) while
the worktree file and the drift-detection digest correctly stay pinned —
producing a run that both truthfully reports "stories keep running under
the pinned snapshot" for the worktree file and, in the same breath,
dispatches a model absent from that snapshot.

Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Confirmed by reading src/theforge/cli/sprint.py, src/theforge/sprint/runner.py, src/theforge/coordinator/config_snapshot.py, and grepping config.assignment usage sites at HEAD during this investigation, cross-checked against the attached run log, pinned snapshot file, root forge.yaml, and routing JSON evidence (all read directly, not assumed).
Support: Direct code trace, independently reproduced during this investigation:
cli/sprint.py loads config from the live root file and passes it into
SprintRunContext before runner.py's capture_or_load/activate ever runs
(runner.py:5486-5497); activate() only toggles
FORGE_SPRINT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT (config_snapshot.py:251-259); that env var's
only consumer repo-wide is sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree
(config_snapshot.py:301-361), which affects only the worktree file, not
the routing config object; and routing's candidate-pool/exploration logic
reads config.assignment, which is the same live-root-loaded config object
(confirmed via direct grep of config.assignment call sites in
preflight.py, review_phase.py, plan_flow.py, engine.py).
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All supporting facts read directly from the current repository source and directly from the attached evidence files during this investigation. A prior diagnosis pass reached the same conclusion; this investigation independently re-derived the call chain from source rather than accepting that prior conclusion at face value, and additionally verified the config.assignment linkage that the prior pass had explicitly left untraced.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:162-182 (config loaded from the live project
root before any pin exists), src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:401-402 and
:1403-1404 (SprintRunContext.for_sprint receives that live-root config),
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:5486-5497 (capture_or_load/activate run
after config is already fixed, and activate() does not refresh it),
src/theforge/coordinator/config_snapshot.py:251-259 (activate, sets only
an env var) and :301-361 (sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree, the pin's sole
actual consumer, worktree-file-only).

### Fix-success criterion

On a resumed sprint where the project-root forge.yaml has drifted from
the pinned snapshot, every model the router selects for any story (dev,
plan, preflight, review-pool candidates, exploration) must be resolvable
from the pinned snapshot's `models` section alone — i.e. an operator who
opens only the pinned .forge/sprints/<id>/forge.yaml must be able to
account for every model_identity recorded in that run's routing/*.json
and audit routing_decision.candidate_pool fields. Concretely: re-run the
same drift scenario (pin, then add a model+exploration change to the root
config, then resume) and confirm no routing artifact for the resumed run
references a model absent from the pinned snapshot.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- sync_forge_yaml_into_worktree silently withdraws the synced forge.yaml when a worktree does not track forge.yaml and skip-worktree fails — a separate, already-documented best-effort fallback (config_snapshot.py:346-359), unrelated to this issue's routing divergence.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Likely fix is to make the ForgeConfig used for routing/dispatch come from
the same source as the worktree sync: either (a) call capture_or_load
before load_config_checked and load the sprint's operative ForgeConfig
from pinned_forge_yaml()/the snapshot path when one exists and is being
reused, or (b) have activate() trigger a re-parse of the pinned file into
a fresh ForgeConfig and thread it back into the sprint context
(_ctx.config) before any routing/dispatch reads it. Not verified against
the full config-plumbing call graph (e.g. ForgeConfig immutability /
dataclasses.replace patterns used elsewhere in sprint.py, such as the
`replace(config, sprint=replace(...))` pattern seen at cli/sprint.py
around line 1396), so treat as a starting point, not a final design.

### Notes

I did not trace the exact function(s) inside routing.py/assignment.py
that assemble the code-review candidate_pool value all the way down to
the JSON key names, but I did independently verify (beyond the prior
diagnosis pass, which left this untraced) that config.assignment — the
AssignmentConfig consumed by assignment.py's candidate-pool/exploration
functions — is read directly off the same `config` object established as
live-root-provenance in cli/sprint.py. This closes the gap the prior
investigation flagged as unconfirmed and supports treating the cause as
fully confirmed rather than partially confirmed.

findings.description: When a sprint's pinned snapshot no longer parses or validates under the running code, the reload of that snapshot raises out of sprint entry as an uncaught exception, so the operator sees a raw traceback instead of the formatted structural-config error and exit code 2 that every other sprint entrypoint produces for an unloadable forge.yaml.

When an operator points a sprint at a configuration file whose name or location is not the project root forge.yaml while a forge.yaml also exists at that root, the run silently adopts the root file's pinned snapshot as its operative configuration and the explicitly supplied file stops influencing model selection.

On a resumed sprint whose root configuration has drifted, the startup credential and binary warnings are computed from the live root configuration's profiles while the run then executes under the pinned snapshot's profiles, so the warnings can describe a model set the run never uses and stay silent about one it does.

finding_registry.description: When a sprint's pinned snapshot no longer parses or validates under the running code, the reload of that snapshot raises out of sprint entry as an uncaught exception, so the operator sees a raw traceback instead of the formatted structural-config error and exit code 2 that every other sprint entrypoint produces for an unloadable forge.yaml.

When an operator points a sprint at a configuration file whose name or location is not the project root forge.yaml while a forge.yaml also exists at that root, the run silently adopts the root file's pinned snapshot as its operative configuration and the explicitly supplied file stops influencing model selection.

On a resumed sprint whose root configuration has drifted, the startup credential and binary warnings are computed from the live root configuration's profiles while the run then executes under the pinned snapshot's profiles, so the warnings can describe a model set the run never uses and stay silent about one it does.

When a daemon-queued sprint's pinned configuration no longer validates, sprint establishment raises SystemExit, which passes straight through the daemon's SprintConflictError and Exception handlers and out of its queue loop, so the sprint is recorded with no completed entry and no crash log while the remaining queued sprints are stranded.

A query-mode sprint that reaches dispatch prints the startup credential and binary warnings twice — once after the pin is established and again after the run context is built — so the operator sees the same warning block duplicated at launch.

When a sprint pins a configuration file whose name is not the project-root forge.yaml, drift detection still compares the pin against the project-root forge.yaml, so the run reports on every entry and before every story that the root file drifted from the pin even though nothing changed, while an actual edit to the file the run pinned goes unreported.

When a manifest-mode sprint fails because its pinned configuration no longer validates, the run's terminal marker is written with the generic placeholder cause 'sprint process ended before recording a completion' rather than the configuration error, so status surfaces name the run as failed for an unknown reason even though the command printed the real cause to stderr.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

steps.details: Immediately after capture_or_load and activate establish the sprint snapshot, reload the operative ForgeConfig from that snapshot path and replace the sprint run context's config before any preflight, planning, review, assignment, or story dispatch code can read _ctx.config. Preserve project_root, sprint metadata, and any existing context fields that are not sourced from forge.yaml by using the repository's existing dataclasses.replace pattern rather than introducing parallel mutable state.

steps.description: Thread the rebuilt config through sprint context consistently
steps.details: Keep CLI startup loading the live root forge.yaml only as the initial bootstrap needed to identify project/sprint context, but make runner startup the authoritative place where the captured or reused sprint snapshot replaces that bootstrap config. Ensure both query-mode and manifest-mode SprintRunContext.for_sprint paths continue to work and converge on the snapshot-backed config during run_sprint.

steps.description: Preserve operator-facing drift reporting while aligning it with routing behavior
steps.details: Leave the existing warning and worktree-sync messages in place when the root forge.yaml differs from the pinned snapshot, but make the same pinned snapshot path also drive the in-memory config reload. Avoid changing the message semantics unless needed to clarify that routing, assignment, and worktree forge.yaml all use the pinned snapshot.

steps.description: Add seam-level regression coverage for resumed drifted config routing
steps.details: Add or extend integration-style tests that create a pinned sprint snapshot, mutate the root forge.yaml to add a model and exploration settings, resume the sprint, and assert the routing config/candidate pool cannot include models absent from the pinned snapshot. Include a focused test that the context config used after runner startup reflects the snapshot file rather than the drifted root file.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A sprint runs under one configuration, and the pinned snapshot reported as authoritative is the configuration every part of that run reads.
The model registry the router selects from, exploration and assignment settings, and forge.yaml synced into each worktree all come from the same pinned snapshot on resumed drifted sprints.
When root config drifts after pinning, the run keeps the snapshot rather than reporting one config while any component reads another.
An audit reader who opens only the pinned .forge/sprints/<id>/forge.yaml can account for every dispatched model_identity and routing_decision candidate_pool model.
Re-run the drift scenario and confirm no routing artifact for the resumed run references a model absent from the pinned snapshot.

risks.description: The initial live-root config may contain CLI bootstrap values that are not present or differ in the pinned snapshot.
risks.mitigation: Reload only after capture_or_load has identified the snapshot, then preserve non-forge.yaml context fields with dataclasses.replace so runtime metadata is not accidentally discarded.

risks.description: Importing CLI config-loading helpers into runner.py could violate layering.
risks.mitigation: Place any shared snapshot config loading helper in a low-dependency config or config_snapshot module rather than making runner.py depend on cli/sprint.py.

risks.description: Existing logs may imply only worktree sync today, so changing config authority without audit visibility could make diagnosis harder.
risks.mitigation: Keep or extend startup/drift logging so the snapshot digest/path used for the in-memory config is visible alongside the existing worktree sync message.
